newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish opposition sees gangster scandal cover up.
newsitem.headline: Turkish opposition sees gangster scandal cover up.

text.p: Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz on Wednesday accused the Islamist-led government of attempting to cover up a scandal over Turkey's alleged use of far-right gangsters to carry out political dirty work.
"It's no coincidence that their attempts to control the judiciary and silence the press come at a time when political dirt has reached such an extreme dimension," Yilmaz said.
The ruling coalition is preparing a bill that is expected to restrict criticism of the government and bureaucrats by Turkey's media, on the trail of an unpleasant scent in the corridors of power.
"Those who want to silence the press are trying to cover their own dirty business, they are afraid of the truth coming out," Motherland Party (ANAP) leader Yilmaz told reporters.
A series of media revelations uncovered a close relationship between late mobster Abdullah Catli and government MP Sedat Bucak, who heads an anti-guerrilla Kurdish militia.
The media has also said that Turkey may have ordered Catli or other rightist mobsters to carry out death squad killings of suspected Kurdish rebel sympathisers and an Armenian guerrilla.
Far from trying to hide the scandal, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller on Tuesday defended the gangster.

"I do not know whether he is guilty or not...But those who fire bullets or suffer their wounds in the name of this country, this nation and this state will always be respectfully remembered by us," she said in a referenc to Catli.
"I don't know Abdullah Catli. But I have investigated. He has no confirmed conviction in Turkey," Ciller, also the foreign minister, told a meeting of her conservative True Path Party.

Catli, once a leading light in the extreme nationalist "Grey Wolf" movement, is also alleged to have helped the Pope's would-be assassin Mehmet Ali Agca escape imprisonment in Turkey before the 1981 attack on the Pontiff.
Convicted drug smuggler Catli and a senior policeman died in the same car in a crash on November 3. MP Bucak, from Ciller's True Path Party, was also in the vehicle.
State officials are alleged to have encouraged criminal gangs to take over the lucrative heroin trade from Kurdish drug barons sympathetic to Kurdistan Workers Party rebels.
"Our people's money is being used as a vehicle for dirty dealings. Dirty money is the foundation of the mafia and these gangs," Yilmaz said.
Former prime minister Yilmaz was punched in a hotel lobby last weekend during a visit to Budapest. His aides have blamed Grey Wolves resident in Hungary for the attack.
President Suleyman Demirel has only half-heartedly called for the scandal to be probed and commentators see the government as unwilling to cooperate.
"It is obvious that the True Path wing of the government will pull out all the stops to cover up the scandal," political analyst Bilal Cetin told Reuters.
"Welfare may try to cover up for the sake of continuing the coalition. They may try to drag it out forever," he said.
The interior minister, who had stayed at the same hotel as the gangster on the weekend of his death, resigned earlier this month.
